mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises real discount rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where FEDFUNDS exceeds 3% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with weakening household demand, which reduces corporate earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1% indicates a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals robust demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12M MA and GDPC1 > 12M MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, which ultimately reduces profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 500K units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn that reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of such episodes.
